propositions: Root disk on autodeploy hosts fills to 92–96% and stays pinned during quiet periods because prune_docker_caches() is only called on deploy and backoff paths, not on the ~2-min no-op ticks when main is quiescent.
The no-op early exit at autodeploy.sh:228 currently returns without pruning, leaving a gap between deploys where accumulated docker artifacts are never reclaimed.

prune_docker_caches() is defined at line ~245, after the no-op exit at line 228, so it cannot be called from the early exit without relocation; moving the definition to the helper block (~150) allows it to be called from line 228 and maintains validity for existing call sites (backoff/deploy paths at 261+).

Adding a pressure-triggered, throttled reclaim on the no-op path with an 80% threshold (below the 85% alarm), 600s minimum interval, and persisted timestamp file will prevent disk overfill during quiescent periods without churning on every tick.
A prune failure on the pressure path must not alter the script's exit code or control flow, only log and emit a countable AUTODEPLOY_DISK_PRESSURE marker.
